title: "Software Fundamentals Matter More Than Ever" — Matt Pocock
talk_summary: Matt Pocock argues that AI-generated code quality collapses without deliberate software design, and that 'specs-to-code' loops produce progressively worse code. He offers concrete skills: relentless plan-grilling to reach a shared design concept, a ubiquitous-language glossary, TDD to force small steps, and refactoring toward deep modules with simple interfaces so agents can navigate and test the codebase.

takeaways.what_they_do: Before writing a plan or PRD, the agent interviews the human relentlessly down each branch of the design tree until a shared understanding is reached, instead of eagerly emitting a plan asset.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Interview me relentlessly about every aspect of this plan until we reach a shared understanding. Walk down each branch of the design tree

takeaways.what_they_do: A skill scans the codebase and generates a markdown glossary of domain terms; that file is passed to the agent and kept open during planning and implementation so code, plans, and discussion share one vocabulary.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it not only improves the planning, but it allows the AI to think in a less verbose way, and actually means that the implementation is more aligned

takeaways.what_they_do: Force the agent to write a failing test first, make it pass, then refactor, because agents otherwise write huge batches of code before checking anything ('outrunning your headlights').
takeaways.evidence_quote: TDD forces the LLM to really take small steps. You create a test first, you make that test pass, and then you refactor

takeaways.what_they_do: Refactor toward few large modules hiding complexity behind simple interfaces, so agents can navigate the codebase and tests can target stable boundaries instead of many shallow modules.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Deep modules, lots of functionality hidden behind a simple interface. Hiding the complexity.

takeaways.what_they_do: Humans/planners own module interfaces and treat implementations as gray boxes verified by tests at the boundary, rather than reviewing every line.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Design the interface, delegate the implementation.

takeaways.what_they_do: Every change considers whole-system design (entropy control) rather than only the local task, preventing codebase degradation across iterations.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Invest in the design of the system every day.
